method: All 48 workbook deterministic checks were applied independently from the frozen workbook procedure and skill guidance. Private client checker executables were not present or executed. Manual source review was supplemented by fresh hash, TOML/JSON parse, bash syntax, line-ending, dependency, prompt-schema, timeout and literal scans. Pass means the documented mechanical condition is established by those observations; it is not a portal-checker or configured-judge result.
measurement_limits: The raw evidence index named by the assignment was absent, and manifest.inputs.review_contract.evidence_index is empty. No configured judge duration, full verifier launch/grade, Oracle score, target-model score, reward discrimination run or reward-ordering run is claimed.

All 43 task files matched the manifest hashes. The private deterministic checker suite was unavailable, so every executable-name verdict below is a manual application unless an actual local parser or shell run is cited.

counterexample_assessment.broken_app_that_could_pass: A server that keeps all saved records only in memory and ignores SIGTERM can remain on port 3000. tests/test.sh:152-181 waits five seconds but never asserts old-group death or escalates to SIGKILL, starts a replacement that can fail EADDRINUSE, and accepts the still-running old server through the generic readiness probe. The restart tool can therefore report success and let the persistence row read memory from the original process.
counterexample_assessment.conforming_app_that_could_fail: A conforming server with a slow or SIGTERM-resistant shutdown handler can make tests/test.sh:33-39 block forever in wait during final cleanup. Separately, the literal XXX sequence at solution/app/package-lock.json:2154 is inside an npm integrity digest, so treating that substring as a template marker would falsely reject a valid pinned lockfile; the manual placeholder verdict excludes that non-semantic digest occurrence.

deterministic.name: check-verifier-contract.py
deterministic.evidence: Static contract basics pass (fresh bash -n, LF-only, zero record at tests/test.sh:60 before grading, EXIT trap at :61, liveness at :115-125, gates-before-scored at :212-227, no shell exec). The lifecycle contract nevertheless fails in three concrete places. Cleanup sends only TERM then performs unbounded wait at :33-39, so a resistant process can hang final verifier exit. Restart sends TERM and waits only five seconds at :152-158, never proves the old group died or sends KILL, starts a replacement at :160-169, then accepts any response on the old URL at :170-181; an old listener can therefore make a failed replacement look ready. Finally, score.py after the gates writes graded=1/no_op=0 at score.py:50-60, but a later scored-suite failure takes test.sh:224-225 without write_zero_reward, leaving that gates-only record to look like a completed grade. The task test.sh hash bd68259276ca4b034654efc8a1723a4e702ed62dbe590af6201565f43eabe5aa equals the frozen template, so this is a shared-policy defect rather than task drift.
deterministic.counterexample: A plausible submission starts a process group whose server keeps its snippet library only in memory, binds port 3000 and ignores SIGTERM. restart_app waits five seconds, starts a replacement that exits EADDRINUSE, probes the surviving old server, reports success and allows the restart persistence criterion to pass without replacement. The same resistant group makes cleanup block forever. Independently, any scored RewardKit timeout after passing gates leaves the gates-only score.py output marked graded=1/no_op=0 instead of the required evaluator-failure plain zero.
deterministic.suggested_fix: Have the shared-harness owner issue a new canonical template that performs bounded TERM then KILL on the old process group, asserts old-group termination and new-PID liveness before readiness, bounds final cleanup, and writes the plain zero on scored-suite failure; freeze a new candidate and run resistant-process/replacement plus full configured verifier controls. Do not patch this candidate's shared file alone.
